subject: Visibility safeguard: EMEA/APAC forecast visibility & final asks
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2026 07:12:00 +0000
Subject: Visibility safeguard: EMEA/APAC forecast visibility & final asks

Team —

Quick one: finance is running a regional consolidation tomorrow and we need a single source-of-truth for what we are counting toward this quarter. I put together a simple commit matrix (attached) — please do the following by EOD Monday, 17 Aug UTC: 

- Update stage to the one you expect me to count (Stage field in the sheet).
- Confirm commit amount (net ARR in GBP where available) and firm close date.
- Add short comment if deal has an open procurement/legal obstacle or needs exec engagement.

Priority: top 12 EMEA/APAC deals (tab "Top Deals"). If you have a revenue split across regions, mark the portion that belongs to EMEA/APAC. Finance will treat any deal without a confirmed stage/commit as "no count".

Attachments: EMEA_APAC_commit_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

Rationale: need to avoid late upward adjustments that blow the commit target. If a customer is still in procurement/legal review with active redlines, flag it — we can coordinate escalation but it must be explicit.

Thanks — I know this is a tight window. Ping me if you need me to call the account owner before the lock.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Director, EMEA Sales
Redwood Inference

- DATW-584 (DataWorks) — customer asked to pause while they do budget confirmation; marking as "No Count" unless we get confirmation by Friday.

Looping in an update on ORION-9231 — procurement returned the contract with two commercial redlines (payment term and liability cap). I attached the redline summary we shared with Legal: OrionTech_contract_redlines.pdf (stub). Procurement is asking for a 60-day payment term and a 12-month auto-renew clause; Legal pushed back on both.

Action items for the matrix:
- I set stage to "Procurement Review" and set commit = GBP 220,000 (probable) but added comment "pending payment term / liability cap resolution".
- For visibility, I added a link to the HubSpot deal (see related links).

If we want this counted as commit, we need either: a finance-approved payment plan (Finance sign-off) or exec outreach to get procurement to accept Net30. I recommend we escalate to the customer C-suite only if Ben wants to pursue an exec-level ask.

Thanks for the updates — appreciate the quick turnaround. Finance will do the lock at 18:00 UTC. Final guidance:

- Anything explicitly marked "Procurement Review" or with unresolved redlines will be treated as "Contingent" and excluded from the hard commit total unless Finance gets an explicit sign-off (finance@redwood.com) by 17:30 UTC.
- Deals marked "Probable" with an assigned close date within the quarter will be included at the amount listed, provided account owner confirms via the matrix comment.

Marissa — please consolidate the final matrix into the Drive link and send me the final totals as a 1-line summary (EMEA total commit / Contingent / Uncounted) before 17:55 UTC so I can sign off and inform Revenue Ops.
